title: Camera holds on its lens

source.why_this_clip: A film camera is seen straight on in close-up, its round lens with ringed bezels filling the centre of the frame, and the camera holds almost still with only slight shifts of the lens and light. Cuts fall at 4.0, 5.75 and 12.0 s, and the earlier studio shot has the camera partly hidden by its operator, so this last 3 s shot is the one where the camera is unobstructed throughout.

source_selection.evidence: Sixteen raw samples show the same frontal camera after the precedingcut. Lens/body stayslarge and cropped; no transition inside12–15. Retained endpoint slightly shortened to the final frozen vector observation; no pose extrapolation.

assembly_summary: Four native strokes keep the box camera and concentric lens. Source is a severe close crop; source controls become separately credited held scene marks. Camera action is a near-hold with slight registration changes, not invented lens spin.
review_note: Bounded repair after independent still critique: Vertically expand the four original camera strokes1.55× and horizontally1.15× around the observed lens center; preserve polygon/open loops and near-held drift.
